items.followUp: A car slows uniformly from 24 m s⁻¹ to 8 m s⁻¹ in 4 s. Find its retardation.

rubric.why: For correctly identifying the given quantities.
rubric.description: States the given initial velocity, final velocity and time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for all three values with units or symbols.

rubric.why: For selecting the acceleration formula.
rubric.description: Uses the formula for acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: For correct substitution and calculation.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values and obtains acceleration of −3 m s⁻².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substitution and 1 mark for the correct result.

rubric.why: For giving retardation as a positive magnitude with the correct unit.
rubric.description: States retardation = 3 m s⁻².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the magnitude and unit.

modelAnswer: Given: initial velocity, u = 30 m s⁻¹; final velocity, v = 15 m s⁻¹; time, t = 5 s.
Acceleration, a = (v − u)/t.
The negative sign shows that the car is slowing down.
Retardation = 3 m s⁻².

items.followUp: Name the three states of equilibrium and define each state.

rubric.why: For naming all three states.
rubric.description: Names stable, unstable and neutral equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when all three names are present.

rubric.why: For the defining behaviour of stable equilibrium.
rubric.description: A slightly displaced body returns to its original position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this definition.

rubric.why: For the defining behaviour of unstable equilibrium.
rubric.description: A slightly displaced body moves farther from its original position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this definition.

rubric.why: For the defining behaviour of neutral equilibrium.
rubric.description: A slightly displaced body remains in its new position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this definition.

modelAnswer: The three states of equilibrium are stable, unstable and neutral equilibrium.
Stable equilibrium: A body slightly displaced from its position returns to its original position.
Unstable equilibrium: A body slightly displaced from its position moves farther away from its original position.
Neutral equilibrium: A body slightly displaced from its position remains in its new position.

items.followUp: A 5 kg load is raised through a vertical height of 4 m. Calculate the work done against gravity. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: For identifying the mass and calculating the total height from the steps.
rubric.description: Finds the total vertical height as 18 × 20 cm = 360 cm = 3.6 m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct height in metres.

rubric.why: For choosing the work-against-gravity formula.
rubric.description: Uses W = mgh.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the formula.

rubric.why: For substituting the values with consistent SI units.
rubric.description: Substitutes m = 10 kg, g = 10 m s⁻² and h = 3.6 m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution.

rubric.why: For calculating and stating the work with its unit.
rubric.description: Obtains 360 J.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the numerical result and 1 mark for the joule unit.

modelAnswer: Given: mass, m = 10 kg; number of steps = 18; height of each step = 20 cm = 0.20 m; g = 10 m s⁻².
Total height, h = 18 × 0.20 = 3.6 m.
Work done against gravity, W = mgh.
W = 10 kg × 10 m s⁻² × 3.6 m = 360 kg m² s⁻².
Work done = 360 J.

items.followUp: Explain how a hydraulic lift multiplies force using Pascal's law.

rubric.why: For stating the relevant principle.
rubric.description: Pascal's law states that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally in all directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the law's key idea.

rubric.why: For identifying the essential parts and their arrangement.
rubric.description: Describes two pistons of different areas connected by an enclosed liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the arrangement.

rubric.why: For relating the pressures at the two pistons.
rubric.description: Uses equal pressure: F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct pressure relation.

rubric.why: For explaining how the press produces a larger output force.
rubric.description: A small force on the smaller piston produces a larger force on the larger piston.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the force-multiplication explanation.

modelAnswer: Pascal's law states that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally in all directions.
A hydraulic press consists of two pistons of different areas connected by an enclosed liquid.
If forces F₁ and F₂ act on pistons of areas A₁ and A₂, respectively, then F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂.
A small force applied to the smaller piston therefore produces a larger force on the larger piston.

items.followUp: Define the least count of a measuring instrument.

rubric.why: For defining least count as the minimum measurable value of an instrument.
rubric.description: The least count is the smallest measurement that an instrument can measure accurately.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a complete definition; 1 mark if it says only that it is the smallest scale division.

modelAnswer: The least count of an instrument is the smallest measurement that it can measure accurately.

rubric.why: For defining the branch concerned with plasma.
rubric.description: Plasma physics is the branch of physics that studies plasma, a gas of charged particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying plasma and its study as a branch of physics.

rubric.why: For defining the branch concerned with the Earth.
rubric.description: Geophysics is the application of physics to the study of the Earth and its physical properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking physics with the study of the Earth.

modelAnswer: Plasma physics is the branch of physics that studies plasma, a gas of charged particles.
Geophysics is the application of physics to the study of the Earth and its physical properties.

items.followUp: Differentiate between fundamental and derived quantities, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: For describing base quantities as independent quantities.
rubric.description: Base quantities are independent quantities that are not defined in terms of other physical quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining distinction.

rubric.why: For describing derived quantities as formed from base quantities.
rubric.description: Derived quantities are obtained by combining base quantities; for example, speed = distance/time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the distinction with an appropriate example.

modelAnswer: Base quantities are independent physical quantities that are not defined in terms of other quantities; for example, length.
Derived quantities are obtained by combining base quantities; for example, speed = distance/time.

rubric.why: For identifying speed as distance travelled per unit time.
rubric.description: Speed is the distance travelled per unit time and is a scalar quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition or distinction identifying speed as scalar.

rubric.why: For identifying velocity as displacement per unit time.
rubric.description: Velocity is displacement per unit time and has a direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition or distinction identifying velocity as directional.

modelAnswer: Speed is the distance travelled per unit time; it is a scalar quantity.
Velocity is the displacement per unit time; it has both magnitude and direction.
